_comment: CLAUDE.md size ratchet CEILING (W1-T503, MASTER-PLAN 8A). capBytes is the only figure declared here -- the actual byte size is measured fresh from the committed CLAUDE.md by `node scripts/claude-md-budget-ratchet.mjs` on every run (W1-T1234: a stored measured figure went stale on every edit to CLAUDE.md and reddened the gate for a reason no PR caused). capBytes carries deliberate headroom over the file's typical size, which is a change from the zero-headroom shape this baseline held until 2026-08-22 -- see bumpRationale for the current raise and priorBumpRationale for the one that retired zero-headroom. IT IS NO LONGER A ROUND BOUNDARY: 65536 (64 KiB) was chosen for legibility on 2026-08-22 and the 2026-08-28 raise traded that legibility for a stated +2000 increment, so do not 'restore' a power of two by rounding this figure in either direction. The ceiling still fails closed and still only ever ratchets UP by a reviewed bump that says why growth is right; never lower it to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules.
bumpRationale: Raised 65536 -> 67536 (+2000) by an OPERATOR DECISION on 2026-08-28. THIS IS THE THIRD CONVERSATION ABOUT THIS NUMBER, and the 2026-08-22 entry (preserved verbatim as priorBumpRationale) set the bar for it: 'the folds are expensive now' carried once and cannot carry twice without new evidence. THE NEW EVIDENCE IS A MEASURED RATE, NOT A FEELING. CLAUDE.md stood at 65488 bytes against the 65536 ceiling -- 48 BYTES FREE -- and a retro on 2026-08-28 harvested rules it could not land: the drafted additions measured +1374, over the cap by 1326, so the run opened NO PR and reported the ceiling as the blocker instead. That is the cost this raise buys off: a ceiling that stops a rule from being written at all is no longer taxing prose, it is dropping knowledge on the floor. THE ARITHMETIC, SAID PLAINLY SO THE NEXT READER CAN CHECK IT: growth has run about 192 bytes/day over the file's lifetime and about 374 bytes/day over the last fortnight, so +2000 buys roughly five days at the recent rate and rather less once this PR's own +1397 is spent -- 67536 - 66885 = 651 BYTES OF HEADROOM THE MOMENT THIS LANDS, under two days at the recent rate. A FOURTH RAISE IS THEREFORE FORESEEABLE AND MUST NOT BE AUTOMATIC; whoever asks for it needs evidence this one did not have. AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN OMITTED, because it is the stronger half of the case against: the cost of a byte in this file is NOT context -- it is COMPETITION TO BE SELECTED. Every rule added makes every other rule marginally less likely to be the one a session reads and acts on, and compression pressure is precisely what has kept this file useful rather than exhaustive. A larger ceiling does not make a rule worth writing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE, unchanged from 2026-08-22: the ratchet still fails closed, still runs unconditionally in ci.yml, and still reports size against cap on every run. NEVER lower capBytes to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules. AND THE FOLD ATTEMPT THIS RAISE IS PREDICATED ON WAS ACTUALLY RUN, for the third time: a 3-word-shingle Jaccard scan over all 82 top-level bullets found a maximum pairwise overlap of 0.0314 (two prior lanes measured 0.083 and 'none'), so no lossless fold exists to take instead. That scan did find one real duplicate and it was TAKEN rather than added: a harvested rule about `grep:` patterns wrapping across physical lines already existed at head, so this PR drops it and lands two changes rather than three.
priorBumpRationale: Raised 62733 -> 65536 (64 KiB) by an OPERATOR DECISION on 2026-08-22, and the reason is the cost of the old shape rather than the size of the file. THE ZERO-HEADROOM CEILING WAS RETIRED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Holding capBytes equal to CLAUDE.md's measured size made every edit pay a fold tax whether or not it had anything left to fold: the file hit the cap with ONE BYTE of room twice on the SAME DAY, and both times the lane spent more effort compressing prose than writing the rule it came to write -- the first paid 283 bytes across nine citation folds, the second paid eleven lines across three more. The cheap folds are spent, so the next fold would have cost meaning rather than duplication. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the ratchet still fails closed, still runs unconditionally in ci.yml, and still reports size against cap on every run. The intent is that an edit DELIBERATES about its own cost, not that every edit pays a tax at the moment it happens. 65536 is chosen as a round, legible boundary rather than an arbitrary figure -- +2803 bytes over the retired cap, roughly six to eight rules at the observed size of that day's additions. AND THIS IS THE SECOND CONVERSATION ABOUT THIS NUMBER, NOT THE FIRST: a later reader proposing another raise should know the operator has already granted one, and should say what changed since -- 'the folds are expensive now' was the argument that carried this time and cannot carry twice without new evidence.
